compare.intro: This unit's points come in look-alike sets: について and に[関|かん]して both give the topic (に[関|かん]して is more formal), while に[対|たい]して aims an action or feeling at someone or sets two facts side by side; にとって gives whose point of view a judgement comes from, として gives a role, and としては gives an opinion from a position; によって says the result changes from case to case, while によっては picks out some cases; [向|む]け is what someone made for a group, and [向|む]き is what suits it.

forms.tag: 見る立場 · for (someone), with a judgement
forms.ja: 朝が弱い私{にとって}、十時からの[授業|じゅぎょう]は[助|たす]かります。
forms.en: For me, as I'm not a morning person, classes from ten o'clock are a real help.

forms.tag: 立場からの意見 · speaking as (an opinion)
forms.ja: 学校{としては}、[授業中|じゅぎょうちゅう]はスマホを使わないでほしいそうです。
forms.en: The school, for its part, would like students not to use their phones in class.

forms.ja: この町の人は、外から来た人{に[対|たい]して}もとても親切です。
forms.en: People in this town are very kind, even to people who come from outside.

check.label: Whose point of view?
check.q: この駅の乗り[換|か]えは、^[初|はじ]めてこの町に来た人^（　　）とても分かりにくいです。
why: に[対|たい]して aims an action or a feeling at someone, like being kind or getting angry. Being hard to follow is not something the station aims at the visitors.
The station is hard to follow when seen from the visitors' side: にとって + a judgement like 分かりにくい.

としては gives an opinion or wish from someone's position, often with と思う or てほしい, or means "for a …" about the person themselves. Here the station is the subject and the visitors give no opinion, so neither fits.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: 学生たちは、新しい図書館の使い方（　　）^説明を[受|う]けました^。
why: に[対|たい]して aims an action or a feeling at a person, or sets two facts side by side. 使い方 is what the talk was about, not someone it was aimed at.
How to use the new library was the topic of the talk: について + 説明を[受|う]ける.
にとって is followed by a judgement seen from someone's side, like 大切だ. A way of using a library has no point of view.
として gives a role or a use, as in カフェとして使う. The way of using the library is not playing a role here.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: ^私^（　　）、来年も同じ先生の[授業|じゅぎょう]を[取|と]りたいと^思っています^。
why: にとって is followed by how something looks from someone's side, like うれしい or [大変|たいへん]だ. It is not followed straight away by that person's own wish, like [取|と]りたいと思っています.
私について means "about me", as a topic of talk. Here the speaker is giving her own wish, not talking about herself as a topic.
As for me, I want the same teacher again: としては gives the speaker's own opinion or wish, and と思っています follows naturally.
によって says that something differs from case to case. There is only one person here, so nothing varies.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: どのクラスに入るかは、^テストの[点数|てんすう]^（　　）[決|き]めます。
why: によっては picks out some cases and is followed by what happens only in them (…こともあります). Here every student is placed by the score, so it does not fit.
[点数|てんすう]について[決|き]める would mean deciding something about the score itself, not deciding the class from it.
に[対|たい]して aims an action or a feeling at someone. A score is not someone the deciding is aimed at.
The class changes with each student's score: によって, "based on, depending on".

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: この動画は、^スマホに[慣|な]れていない人^（　　）^作られて^います。
why: Someone made the video with these users in mind: [向|む]けに + 作られる.
にとって is followed by a judgement, like 分かりやすい. 作られています tells who made it and for whom, not a judgement.
[向|む]き says that something happens to suit a group. When someone made a thing for a group, use [向|む]け.
に[対|たい]して aims an action or a feeling at a person, like speaking politely or being strict. It does not say who a thing was made for.

drill.label: Build the sentence
drill.after: 家族が[一番|いちばん]です。
drill.hint: によって joins a noun and is followed by a word like [違|ちが]う. Which tile says whose view the last part comes from?
drill.full: 何が大切かは人によって{[違|ちが]いますが}私にとっては家族が[一番|いちばん]です。
drill.explain: 人, によって, [違|ちが]いますが, 私にとっては. によって goes on 人 and is followed by [違|ちが]います: what matters differs from person to person. にとっては then gives the speaker's own view: for me, family comes first.

drill.label: Build the sentence
drill.after: メールで[受|う]け[付|つ]けることもあります。
drill.hint: に[関|かん]しては follows the topic noun. Which tile picks out some cases, ready for こともあります?
drill.full: レポートの出し方{に[関|かん]しては}先生によってはメールで[受|う]け[付|つ]けることもあります。
drill.explain: 出し方, に[関|かん]しては, 先生, によっては. レポートの出し方 is the topic, and に[関|かん]しては marks it in a formal way. 先生によっては picks out some teachers, and こともあります at the end fits it: some teachers also accept reports by email.

exam.label: Choose the form
exam.q: 田中さんはチームのリーダー（　　）、みんなの意見をよくまとめている。
exam.explain: として gives Tanaka's role: as the team leader, he brings everyone's views together well. にとって needs a judgement seen from someone's side, not what that person does. に対して would make the leader the person an action is aimed at, but Tanaka is the one acting. 向けに says who a thing was made for.

exam.label: Choose the form
exam.q: この会社では、毎年春に、新しく入った社員（　　）パソコン教室を開いている。
exam.explain: The company runs the class with new staff in mind, so 向けの: made for a group. 向きの is for what happens to suit a group, not for something someone set up for them. としての would make the staff a role the class plays. についての would make the new staff the topic the class teaches.

exam.label: Build the sentence
exam.after: やさしすぎるかもしれない。
exam.full: このクラスは初めて習う人向けなので{経験のある人}にとってはやさしすぎるかもしれない。
exam.explain: 習う人, 向けなので, 経験のある人, にとっては. 初めて習う人向け says who the class was made for, and なので gives the reason. 経験のある人にとっては gives the point of view of the judgement やさしすぎる: for people who have learnt before, it may be too easy.

scene.en: The timetable and course list at a Japanese language school
scene.intro: Tap each word on the course list that a new student needs to plan the term.

check.label: How the exam asks it
check.q: 明日の授業は_欠席します_。
options: 明日の授業におくれます。
明日の授業で発表します。
明日の授業の前に予習します。
明日の授業は休みます。
check.explain: 欠席する means not going to a class or meeting you should attend, so 休みます is closest. おくれます means arriving late, so the speaker still goes. 発表します means giving a talk in the class. 予習します means preparing before the class, and says nothing about missing it.

skill.ask: Which room may Kimura's group use, and which rules change the price?
skill.passage:
さくら市民ホール　部屋を借りる方へ
部屋の料金（一回）
A室（20人まで）1,000円
B室（40人まで）2,000円
C室（80人まで）4,000円
・一回は、午前・午後・夜のどれか一つです。
・^土曜日と日曜日は、どの部屋も料金が500円高くなります^。
・^音楽の練習に使えるのは、C室だけです^。
・^グループの半分以上が市内に住んでいる場合は、料金が半額になります^。
・予約は、使う日の一か月前から、ホールの受付でできます。電話では予約できません。
skill.strategy: Find the room first from what the group will do, then check the day and how many members live in the city.

item.q: 木村さんは、日曜日の午後、友だちと音楽の練習をしたいと思っています。グループは25人で、市内に住んでいるのは10人です。部屋の料金はいくらですか。
item.explain: Music practice is allowed only in room C, which costs 4,000 yen. The practice is on a Sunday, so every room costs 500 yen more: 4,500 yen. Only 10 of the 25 members live in the city, less than half, so there is no half price.
why: This is room C without the weekend rule. On Saturdays and Sundays every room costs 500 yen more.
Room B holds 40 people, but music practice is allowed only in room C.
The half price is only for groups where at least half the members live in the city. 10 of 25 is less than half.
